title: Nothing but Christ and Him Crucified
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Health, intellect and discipline can vanish in a moment. Every day we decide where to put our trust. Let it be Christ and his cross.
exhortation: Lord, we resolve to know nothing but Jesus Christ and him crucified. Forgive us for how easily we trust in things that can be taken away in a moment. Do we trust in our health and physical strength? In our intellect and ability to reason? In our skill and how disciplined we can be? These things can vanish in a flash. They are fool's gold.

Paul knew they wouldn't last. He knew it was fleeting to trust in any earthly thing, and many of them were taken from him. Yet by the power of the Spirit, God used him mightily as his resolve hardened to know nothing but Jesus Christ and his cross.

Every day there is a decision to make: where will we put our trust? It starts with the first thoughts that enter our minds when we wake. What will we dwell on? What will we allow to consume our thinking? Will it be our own comfort and well-being, as if we were narcissists obsessed with ourselves, which I certainly can be every day? Even kingdom work, even pastors doing the work of the kingdom, can become about ourselves if we aren't seeking to make God's glory known. We have to ask ourselves: are we putting ourselves at the center of the universe?

Lord, search us. Show us where we have placed our faith in anything other than your finished work. Steer us by your word and lead us along the path of righteousness, empowered by your Spirit to trust you radically. Give us strength today to put our trust in you even in our weakness, so that like Paul we can say we desire to know nothing but Christ and him crucified. Let this be our boast.
prayer: Lord, remind us again of the time you saved us and opened our eyes, of those moments we stood in awe of your grace and mercy toward us with hearts full of gratitude. Keep us from straying from the truths that set us free.

Keep us from trying to smuggle in our own works, our own eloquence or our own power. Let us rest completely on your grace and your blood shed for us: a truth so simple a child can understand it, and so deep we'll never reach the bottom. Fill our hearts with wonder at your gospel once again. In Jesus' name.
